posts.title: Keep the point. Explore the detail.
posts.anchor: The original idea stays in view while you decide how deep to go.

steps.label: The idea
steps.title: A place to return to.
steps.body: Keep the main point above. Explore the explanation below. If your attention drifts, the starting point is still there.
steps.qualification: A design choice to try, rather than a promise about how everyone reads.
steps.support: The author brief asks for pinned context and an independently scrollable explanation.
steps.sourceLocator: Sections 7–8: pinned context and visual/text relationship

steps.label: More depth
steps.title: You choose how much.
steps.body: One clear point can be enough. Continue for the reasoning, open its supporting material, or leave for a different topic. There is no completion target.
steps.qualification: Important qualifications belong beside the point they qualify.
steps.support: The brief describes finite explanations, optional depth and evidence on demand.
steps.sourceLocator: Sections 2–3 and 12: finite reading, editorial identity and evidence

steps.label: Your place
steps.title: Continue where you left off.
steps.body: Save a post when it is useful. This prototype remembers its current explanation on this device, separately from whether you have read or downloaded it.
steps.qualification: Clearing browser data can remove local preferences and favourites.
steps.support: The brief separates favourites, reading progress and downloaded content.

posts.title: The detail is there when you want it.
posts.topic: Evidence without the wall of text
posts.anchor: A short explanation can lead to useful backing without burying the point.

steps.label: The idea
steps.title: A small plus. A useful explanation.
steps.body: Open the plus for what supports the current point, why it matters and where to read the original material. Close it and return to the same place.
steps.qualification: The demo source is a product brief, not scientific evidence.
steps.support: Section 12 specifies expandable support, full source titles, locators and limits.

steps.label: The backing
steps.title: A title that tells you something.
steps.body: A source should have its full title and a relevant section or passage. The explanation around the link should tell you what it supports, rather than leaving you to guess.
steps.qualification: A source being linked does not mean it supports every possible interpretation.
steps.support: The evidence-panel requirements distinguish a supporting passage from an unexplained link.
steps.sourceLocator: Section 12: meaningful titles and passage locators

steps.label: The return
steps.title: Depth without a detour.
steps.body: Keep the original idea visible. Open the backing beside it or in a sheet. The interface should help you move between the point and its support.
steps.qualification: External documents need a connection unless a permitted copy is included.
steps.support: The brief requires preserved reading context when opening and closing evidence.
steps.sourceLocator: Sections 8, 12 and 23: context and return behaviour

posts.title: Make the space yours.
posts.anchor: The reading surface should adapt to you, with the controls available when needed.

steps.label: The idea
steps.title: Less furniture. More room.
steps.body: The divider is also a doorway to the controls. Tap it for layout options. Drag it to give either panel more room. Buttons and keyboard controls remain available.
steps.qualification: Dragging is optional; essential actions need another route.
steps.support: The brief requires adjustable split panels and accessible alternatives to dragging.
steps.sourceLocator: Sections 7 and 11: accessible split controls and navigation

steps.label: Your setup
steps.title: Choose a calmer surface.
steps.body: Change the colours, enlarge the text or use a plain opaque finish. The same content can become a continuous article or a compact series of expandable explanations.
steps.qualification: Custom colours still need readable text and clear focus indicators.
steps.support: The brief separates layout from appearance and asks for free persistent preferences.
steps.sourceLocator: Sections 10, 14 and 17: layouts, themes and accessibility

steps.label: The finish
steps.title: Keep what works for you.
steps.body: Your choices stay on this device. Accounts, cross-device syncing, audio and community features are later possibilities; they are not needed to use this reader.
steps.qualification: This comparison is a reading prototype, not a finished app release.
steps.support: The release boundaries keep optional services separate from the core reader.
steps.sourceLocator: Sections 2, 16 and 25: local use and optional future services
